title: An answer to a review request wakes the agent that asked
description:
When a run ends `asked`, the review request names the run and the agent. A person's answer (approve, reject, feedback) is a change that wakes that agent with the answer; the run re-reads the records and continues or stops. The request's `appliedIn` names the run that used the answer. Nothing holds a session open while waiting, and a person who never answers blocks only that one item.

**Acceptance criteria**
- An approval continues the work once.
- Feedback reaches the next run as input.
- An unanswered request blocks nothing else.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- ask-and-answer.feature: an approval wakes the asker and the work completes; a rejection ends it with the reason; feedback is in the next run's input; another Story proceeds while one waits.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Work items and handoffs between agents and people. Slice code F4 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
